title: What is dark matter?
subtitle: Invisible cosmos
subject: sciences
description: We never saw her. Yet without it, galaxies would fall apart. Dark matter is the invisible glue of the Universe.

hero.hook: Imagine an invisible glue that holds galaxies together. We don't see her, but we see what she is holding back.

blocks.text: You feel the wind without seeing it: the branches move, the hair flies. **dark matter** is a bit like that on the scale of the cosmos. It does not shine, does not reflect light, does not block any rays. We only “see” it by what it makes move.
It would represent approximately **27%** of the Universe, five times more than all ordinary matter: stars, planets, gas. Without it, galaxies would spin too fast to hold together.

sections.title: Stars too fast on the outskirts

blocks.text: In the years **1970**, the American astronomer **Vera Rubin** measured the speed of stars in spiral galaxies. In the Solar System, the farther we go from the Sun, the slower we rotate. She expected the same pattern.

blocks.caption: Dark matter betrays its presence through its gravitational effect on galaxy clusters.

blocks.text: Now the stars on the edge were turning **as quickly** as those in the center. With just the visible mass, they should have flown away. It was therefore necessary to have an invisible mass, a **halo**, an invisible spherical envelope around the galaxy, to hold them back.  has become the flagship proof of dark matter. [[The galaxy rotation curve]]
Vera Rubin has long had to fight to be taken seriously. Princeton refused her a doctorate in astronomy for a long time… because she was a woman, until 1975.

sections.title: What is it made of? We are still looking

blocks.text: It is not ordinary matter, called **baryonic**, composed of protons and neutrons: it does not interact with light. It crosses the Earth and us without leaving a visible trace.

The long-favored lead, the **WIMP**, a weakly interacting massive particle, would be a heavy particle outside of , the theory that describes known elementary particles. **liquidxeon** detectors, buried underground, are hoping for a rare shock. Without clear success for the moment. Others rely on the **axion**, an ultra-light particle, or on a gravity to be reviewed. sections.title: And dark energy, the other mystery

blocks.text: Dark matter attracts. The , discovered in **1998**, does the opposite: it accelerates the **expansion of the Universe**, the increasing distance of the galaxies. Galaxies are moving away faster and faster, while gravity should slow down the movement. [[Dark energy]]
It would weigh approximately **68%** of the cosmos. With dark matter, this makes **95%** of invisible Universe. Everything we see, atoms and light, is just a scum of **5 %**.
In the very distant future, dark energy could push other galaxies away to the point of making them invisible from the Milky Way: an almost empty sky.

On the one hand, indirect evidence is accumulating: galactic rotations, **cosmic microwave background**, fossil radiation from the young universe, filament structure of the Universe. On the other hand, no direct particle detection.

The 21st century will have to decide: a new family of particles, or a new way of thinking about gravity. Dark matter is not just a detail of the sky. It is the laboratory where the physics of tomorrow is invented.
Dark matter forms **27 %** of the Universe. It is proven by its gravity on stars and light, even if we have never seen it directly.
